paragraphs: William Russell Kelly pioneered the staffing industry when he founded Kelly® in 1946 and we've been reinventing it ever since. Our inception helped usher in and embolden a workforce of women who kept the economy moving forward during World War II, opening doors and creating completely new opportunities. Over the next 79 years, as work evolved, Kelly continued to equip people with the skills to master new technologies as they emerged and the opportunity to put them to work in ways that enriched their lives.

As the world of work has evolved, so have our offerings to reflect the changing needs of employers and talent. In 1996, Kelly established the industry's first Managed Service Provider ("MSP") program. Three years later, the Company launched specialized offerings in engineering, information technology and education. After successfully establishing industry-leading positions in each of these attractive markets, Kelly initiated a strategic plan to drive greater value creation by refocusing its portfolio on specialties. In 2020, Kelly launched a new operating model comprising five specialty business units: Kelly Professional & Industrial ("P&I"); Kelly Science, Engineering & Technology ("SET"); Kelly Education; KellyOCG ("Outsourcing & Consulting" or "OCG"); and Kelly International.

To enhance specialization in higher margin, higher growth specialties, Kelly also pursued an aggressive approach to driving inorganic growth in SET, Education and OCG. By monetizing non-core assets (Persol Holdings Co., Ltd. in 2022 and EMEA staffing operations in 2024, among other transactions) and redeploying available capital, Kelly completed several strategic acquisitions over the years, including Teachers On Call; Global Technology Associates ("GTA"); NextGen; Greenwood/Asher & Associates; Softworld; RocketPower; Pediatric Therapeutic Services ("PTS"); Motion Recruitment Partners ("MRP"); and Children's Therapy Center ("CTC").

Building on a significant shift in Kelly's business mix driven by its specialty strategy, the Company took steps to further optimize its operating model and accelerate profitable growth. Beginning in 2023, Kelly implemented a comprehensive business transformation initiative that delivered structural efficiency improvements across the enterprise and significantly improved profitability. In 2024, Kelly completed the sale of its European staffing operations within the Company's International business unit, further sharpening its focus on specialty outcome-based and staffing services in North America, while maintaining global recruitment process outsourcing ("RPO") and MSP capabilities. In 2025, Kelly integrated its P&I and OCG specialty areas, responding to a shift in large enterprise demand toward integrated workforce solutions and enabling a more streamlined and efficient go-to-market approach. In addition, the Company launched a multi-year strategic initiative to integrate all of the businesses into one enterprise system. The first phase of integrating the SET business was completed and went live in early 2026.

Today, Kelly remains one of the largest providers of temporary and permanent staffing services, outcome-based solutions, RPO, MSP and payroll process outsourcing ("PPO"). The Company delivers these differentiated offerings through three specialty business units, each a leader in the respective markets on which they are focused: Kelly Education; Kelly Science, Engineering & Technology; and Kelly Enterprise Talent Management.

We strive to empower organizations and talent to access limitless opportunities by enabling employers to recruit and manage skilled workers and help job seekers find great work. As experts in hiring experts, we ensure our customers have the people they need when and where they're needed most. We're also using our position in the middle of the talent supply and demand equation to challenge outdated barriers that hold back far too many people from attaining meaningful work, supporting their families and contributing to the economy. Our Equity@Work initiative seeks to remove barriers to employment and create a labor market that is accessible for more people. While universal change takes time, we continue to make progress with additional outreach, new alliances and partnerships and continued executive commitment.
We believe that delivering on these objectives will result in successful outcomes for customers and talent and drive profitable growth for Kelly.

Kelly is a global specialty talent solutions company operating in three specialized business units, which are also our reportable segments. This structure enables the Company to serve the specialized needs of both talent and customers while building deep industry expertise and connections.

•Enterprise Talent Management – delivers temporary staffing, outcome-based and permanent placement services focused on light industrial, contact center and office and clerical specialties in North America across a variety of industries and includes products such as Business Process Outsourcing, KellyConnect and Skilled Professional Solutions offerings. ETM also provides global talent supply chain and workforce talent solutions, including MSP, RPO and PPO solutions to customers on a global basis. RPO includes our RocketPower and Sevenstep brands as well as our proprietary technology platform, Kelly Helix.

•Science, Engineering & Technology – provides highly specialized skills to a variety of industries through temporary staffing, outcome-based and permanent placement services. SET is focused on science and clinical research, engineering, technology and telecommunications specialties predominantly in North America. It includes the MRP, Softworld, NextGen and GTA brands, as well as our statementworX offering.

•Education – delivers high quality education and therapy services talent through temporary staffing, permanent placement and executive search services to Pre-K-12 school districts and education organizations across the U.S. It includes the CTC, PTS, Greenwood/Asher and Teachers On Call brands.

Financial information regarding our reportable segments is included in the Segment Disclosures footnote in the notes to our consolidated financial statements presented in Part II, Item 8 of this report.

Headquartered in the United States, Kelly provides workforce solutions to a diverse group of local, regional and global clients in the Americas, Europe and the Asia-Pacific region across a variety of industries.
In 2025, together with our supplier partners, we placed approximately 375,000 workers with a variety of customers around the globe.

headings: Risks Related to Macroeconomic Conditions
Our business is significantly affected by fluctuations in general economic conditions.
Our stock price may be subject to significant volatility and could suffer a decline in value.
Risks Related to our Industry Segment
We operate in a highly competitive industry with low barriers to entry and may be unable to compete successfully against existing or new competitors.
Technological advances, including advances in automation and artificial intelligence, may significantly disrupt the labor market and weaken demand for human capital.
Competition rules arising from government legislation, litigation or regulatory activity may limit how we structure and market our services.
Unexpected changes in claim trends on our workers' compensation, unemployment, disability, medical benefit plans, and other expenses may negatively impact our financial condition.
We may have additional tax liabilities that exceed our estimates.
Risks Related to Strategy and Execution
Our future performance depends on the Company's effective execution of our business strategy.
If we fail to successfully improve or develop new service offerings, we may be unable to retain and acquire customers, resulting in a decline in revenues.
A loss of major customers or a change in such customers' buying behavior or economic strength could have a material adverse effect on our business.
We are at risk of damage to our brands, which are important to our success.
We are increasingly dependent on third parties for the execution of critical functions and could be liable for their inability to perform or adhere to global compliance standards.
Our information technology strategy may not yield its intended results.
Past and future acquisitions may not be successful.
Risks Related to Operating a Global Enterprise
Our international operations subject us to potential liability under anti-bribery, anti-corruption, anti-trafficking, supply chain, trade protection and other laws and regulations.
Events such as natural disasters, severe weather, terrorist attacks, war, pandemics and other catastrophic events could decrease demand for our services in impacted areas.
We are subject to substantial pressure to meet external stakeholder's sustainability requirements.
Risks Related to Human Capital
We depend on our ability to attract, develop and retain qualified permanent full-time employees.
We depend on the ability of Kelly and third-party talent suppliers to attract and retain qualified personnel to provide our services.
We may be exposed to employment-related claims and losses, including class action lawsuits and collective actions, which could have a material adverse effect on our business.
Risks Related to Cyber Security and Data Privacy
Damage to our data facilities could affect our ability to sustain critical business applications.
A failure to maintain the privacy of personal data entrusted to us could have significant adverse consequences.
Risks Related to Our Capital Structure
Our controlling stockholder exercises voting control over our company and has the ability to elect or remove from office all of our directors.
We are not subject to certain of the listing standards that normally apply to companies whose shares are quoted on the Nasdaq Global Select Market.
The holders of shares of our Class A common stock are not entitled to voting rights.
Provisions in our certificate of incorporation and bylaws and Delaware law may delay or prevent an acquisition of our Company.
We may not be able to realize value from, or otherwise preserve and utilize, our tax credit and net operating loss carryforwards.
Failure to maintain specified financial covenants in our bank credit facilities
paragraphs: Historically, the general level of economic activity and employment in the United States and the other countries in which we operate has significantly affected the demand for staffing services. In periods of economic growth, employers often add temporary employees before hiring full-time employees. However, when economic activity declines, many employers reduce their use of temporary employees before laying off full-time employees. Customer responses to real or perceived economic conditions, including perceptions related to market conditions, labor supply, international trade policy, and inflation, could negatively impact customer behavior. Historically, significant changes in economic activity have disproportionately impacted staffing industry volumes. We may not fully benefit from times of increased economic activity should we experience shortages in the supply of workers. We may also experience more competitive pricing pressure and slower customer payments during periods of economic decline. A substantial portion of our revenues and earnings are generated by our business operations in the United States. Any significant economic downturn in the United States or certain other countries in which we operate could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

The market price of our common stock may be subject to significant volatility. We believe that many factors, including several which are beyond our control, have a significant effect on the market price of our common stock. These include:
•actual or anticipated variations in our quarterly operating results; •announcements of new services by us or our competitors;
•announcements relating to strategic relationships, acquisitions or divestitures; •changes in financial estimates by securities analysts;
•changes in general economic conditions; •actual or anticipated changes in laws and government regulations;
•commencement of, or involvement in, litigation;

paragraphs: In 2025, Kelly continued to advance its multi-year transformation, building on the decisive actions taken in 2023 and 2024 to streamline the portfolio, sharpen strategic focus, and expand into higher-margin, higher-growth specialties. We remained focused on capturing a greater share of growth, converting a higher proportion of revenue into bottom-line performance, and positioning Kelly to benefit from an eventual recovery in the staffing environment.

Kelly entered 2025 with a simplified operating model concentrated on North American staffing, business process outsourcing ("BPO") and specialty solutions and global Managed Service Provider ("MSP") and recruitment process outsourcing ("RPO") offerings, following the 2024 sale of its European staffing operations and the Ayers Group and acquisition of Motion Recruitment Partners ("MRP") and Children's Therapy Center ("CTC"). These portfolio actions reflected a deliberate shift toward businesses with more attractive growth profiles, scalable platforms, and improved EBITDA margin potential.

We continued to execute our refreshed go-to-market strategy, designed to deliver the full suite of Kelly solutions to large enterprise customers and capture a greater share of wallet while maintaining high service levels for customers of all sizes. This strategy was supported by ongoing commitment to delivering greater effectiveness and data-driven sales processes and initiatives.

Critical to positioning Kelly for future growth was the hiring of Chris Layden as President and Chief Executive Officer in September 2025. Layden succeeded Peter Quigley, who announced his intention to retire in February 2025. Layden brings dynamic industry leadership and extensive experience leading organizations through periods of significant change, while delivering growth and strengthening competitive positioning. Layden's hiring underscores Kelly's commitment to enhancing its operational capabilities and service delivery while transforming its technology processes and platforms.

During 2025, Kelly faced a dynamic macroeconomic environment characterized by sluggish labor market demand and policy shifts which had significant impacts on the industry, including Kelly. In the face of these headwinds, Kelly demonstrated measurable progress in cost discipline and selective market strength. At the same time, we accelerated structural and demand-driven cost optimization initiatives, including technology modernization, acquisition integration and process efficiencies to enhance execution and agility while positioning Kelly to capture market share and improve profitability when staffing market conditions stabilize.

Structural cost actions, operating model simplification, acquisition integration and portfolio reshaping are expected to support continued improvement in Kelly's growth prospects and financial profile as we move through 2026 and beyond.

paragraphs: William Russell Kelly 在 1946 年創立 Kelly® 時，奠定了人力派遣產業的基礎，我們自那時起便持續革新這個產業。我們的成立有助於引進並鼓舞在第二次世界大戰期間推動經濟前進的女性 workforce，為她們打開大門並創造全新的機會。接下來的 79 年，隨著工作的演進，Kelly 也持續協助人們掌握新興科技的技能，並提供機會讓他們以豐富生活的方式運用這些技能。

隨著工作世界的演進，我們的產品與服務也持續調整以反映僱主與人才的變遷需求。1996 年，Kelly 建立了產業內第一個 Managed Service Provider（"MSP"）計畫。三年後，本公司推出了專門的工程、資訊科技與教育服務。在成功建立這些有吸引力市場的產業領導地位後，Kelly 發起了一項戰略計畫，透過重新聚焦於專業領域，以創造更高的價值。2020 年，Kelly 發起了一個包含五個專業業務單位的新營運模式：Kelly Professional & Industrial（"P&I"）；Kelly Science, Engineering & Technology（"SET"）；Kelly Education；KellyOCG（"Outsourcing & Consulting" 或 "OCG"）；以及 Kelly International。

為加強在高毛利率、高成長專業領域的專業化，Kelly 也採用了積極的策略來推動 SET、Education 和 OCG 的無形成長。透過處置非核心資產（如 2022 年的 Persol Holdings Co., Ltd. 和 2024 年的 EMEA 人力派遣業務，以及其他交易），並重新配置可用資本，Kelly 在多年來完成了多項戰略收購，包括 Teachers On Call；Global Technology Associates（"GTA"）；NextGen；Greenwood/Asher & Associates；Softworld；RocketPower；Pediatric Therapeutic Services（"PTS"）；Motion Recruitment Partners（"MRP"）；以及 Children's Therapy Center（"CTC"）。

在 Kelly 的業務組成因專業策略而產生重大轉變的基礎上，本公司採取了進一步優化營運模式並加速獲利成長的步驟。自 2023 年起，Kelly 開始實施一項全面的業務轉型計畫，為企業帶來結構性效率提升，並顯著改善獲利能力。2024 年，Kelly 完成了出售其國際業務單位內的歐洲人力派遣業務，進一步強化其在北美地區的專業成果導向與人力派遣服務的專注，同時維持全球招聘流程外包（"RPO"）與 MSP 能力。2025 年，Kelly 整合了其 P&I 與 OCG 專業領域，回應大型企業需求向整合式 workforce 解決方案的轉變，並啟動更簡潔高效的市場接觸方式。此外，本公司啟動了一項多年期的戰略計畫，以整合所有業務至一個企業系統。SET 業務整合的第一階段已在 2026 年初完成並啟用。

目前，Kelly 仍是全球最大規模的臨時與永久人力派遣服務、成果導向解決方案、RPO、MSP 以及薪資流程外包（"PPO"）提供者之一。本公司透過三個專業業務單位提供這些差異化的服務，每個單位在其專注市場中都是領導者：Kelly Education；Kelly Science, Engineering & Technology；以及 Kelly Enterprise Talent Management。

我們致力於協助組織與人才接觸無限的機會，透過協助僱主招募與管理具備技能的員工，並協助求職者找到理想的工作。作為聘僱專家的專家，我們確保客戶在最需要的時候與地點獲得所需的人力。我們也利用在人才供應與需求之間的中間位置，挑戰那些阻礙太多人獲得有意義工作、支持家庭並為經濟做出貢獻的過時障礙。我們的 Equity@Work 初步計畫旨在消除就業障礙，並建立一個更易於進入的勞動市場。雖然全面性的改變需要時間，我們持續透過更多的宣傳、新的聯盟與合作夥伴關係，以及持續的高階管理層承諾，推動進步。
我們相信實現這些目標將為客戶與人才帶來成功結果，並為 Kelly 帶來獲利成長。
Kelly 是一家全球專業人才解決方案公司，經營三個專業業務單位，這些也是我們的應報告分部。這種結構使本公司能夠同時服務人才與客戶的專業需求，並建立深厚的產業專業知識與聯繫。

•企業人才管理 – 提供臨時人力派遣、以成果為導向及永久安置服務，專注於輕工業、客服中心及辦公室與事務性專業領域，服務範圍遍及北美各產業，包含產品如業務流程外包（Business Process Outsourcing）、KellyConnect 以及專業人才解決方案（Skilled Professional Solutions）等。ETM 還提供全球人才供應鏈及人力資產解決方案，包括 MSP、RPO 與 PPO 解決方案，服務全球客戶。RPO 包含我們的 RocketPower 與 Sevenstep 品牌，以及我們的專有技術平台 Kelly Helix。
•科學、工程與科技 – 透過臨時人力派遣、以成果為導向及永久安置服務，為各產業提供高度專業化的技能。SET 重點在於科學與臨牀研究、工程、科技與電信業專業領域，主要服務範圍為北美。包含 MRP、Softworld、NextGen 與 GTA 品牌，以及我們的 statementworX 解決方案。
•教育 – 透過臨時人力派遣、永久安置及高階人才搜尋服務，為美國 Pre-K-12 學區與教育機構提供高品質的教育與療育服務人才。包含 CTC、PTS、Greenwood/Asher 與 Teachers On Call 品牌。
有關我們應報告分部的財務資訊，請參閱本報告 Part II, Item 8 所列之整併財務報表附註中的 Segment Disclosures 註腳。
本公司總部設於美國，為美洲、歐洲及亞太地區的各類產業客戶提供多元化的 workforce 解決方案。
2025 年，與我們的供應鏈夥伴合作，我們為全球各類客戶安置了約 375,000 名工作者。

paragraphs: 2025 年，Kelly 繼續推動其多年度轉型計畫，建立在 2023 年及 2024 年所採取的關鍵行動基礎上，以簡化產品組合、強化戰略重點，並拓展至毛利率較高、成長較快的專業領域。我們持續專注於掌握更大的成長機會，將更高比例的營業收入轉化為淨利表現，並使 Kelly 能夠受益於就業市場最終復甦的環境。

Kelly 以簡化後的營運模式邁入 2025 年，專注於北美就業服務、業務流程外包（"BPO"）及專業解決方案，以及全球 Managed Service Provider（"MSP"）及招聘流程外包（"RPO"）服務，此為 2024 年出售其歐洲就業服務業務及 Ayers Group 並收購 Motion Recruitment Partners（"MRP"）及 Children's Therapy Center（"CTC"）後的結果。這些產品組合的調整反映了有意圖的轉向成長潛力更佳、可擴展平台及改善 EBITDA 毛利率潛力的業務。
我們持續執行更新後的市場進入策略，旨在向大型企業客戶提供完整的 Kelly 解決方案，並掌握更大的客戶支出份額，同時維持對所有規模客戶的高服務水準。此策略由持續投入提升效益及數據驅動的銷售流程與專案所支撐。

對 Kelly 未來成長至關重要的，是於 2025 年 9 月聘任 Chris Layden 為總裁及首席執行長。Layden 接替 Peter Quigley，後者於 2025 年 2 月宣佈將退休。Layden 帶來動態的產業領導力及豐富的經驗，領導組織經歷重大變革的過程，同時實現成長並強化競爭優勢。Layden 的聘任凸顯 Kelly 提升營運能力與服務交付，同時轉型其資訊科技流程與平台的承諾。
2025 年，Kelly 面對一個動態的總體經濟環境，特徵為就業市場需求疲軟及政策變動，對產業，包括 Kelly，產生顯著影響。面對這些挑戰，Kelly 展現出可衡量的成本控制進展及選擇性市場強勢。同時，我們加速結構性及需求驅動的成本優化專案，包括資訊科技現代化、收購整合及流程效率提升，以強化執行力與靈活性，並使 Kelly 能夠在就業市場條件穩定時掌握市佔率並改善獲利能力。
結構性成本措施、營運模式簡化、收購整合及產品組合調整，預期將支持 Kelly 在 2026 年及以後的成長前景與財務表現持續改善。

headings: 與總體經濟條件相關的風險
本公司營運受總體經濟條件波動顯著影響。
本公司股票價格可能面臨顯著波動，並可能導致股價下跌。
與本公司產業分部相關的風險
本公司所處產業為高度競爭性，且進入門檻低，可能無法成功與現有或新興競爭者競爭。
科技進步，包括自動化及人工智慧的發展，可能顯著幹擾勞動市場，並削弱對人力資本的需求。
因政府立法、訴訟或監管活動所產生的競爭規則，可能限制本公司如何結構及行銷其服務。
本公司員工補償、失業、殘障、醫療福利計畫及其他費用的聲請趨勢出現意外變動，可能對本公司財務狀況造成負面影響。
我們可能有額外的稅務負擔，超過我們的預估。
與策略及執行相關的風險
我們未來的表現取決於本公司有效執行商業策略的能力。
若我們未能成功改善或開發新的服務方案，我們可能無法保留及獲取客戶，導致營收下降。
主要客戶流失或客戶購買新行為或經濟實力改變，可能對我們的業務造成重大不利影響。
我們的商標可能受到損害，而商標對我們的成功至關重要。
我們越來越依賴第三方執行關鍵功能，可能因第三方無法履行或遵循全球合規標準而負起責任。
我們的資訊科技策略可能無法達到預期的結果。
過去及未來的併購可能無法成功。
與經營全球企業相關的風險

天然災害、嚴峻天氣、恐怖攻擊、戰爭、疫情及其他災難性事件可能降低我們服務在受影響地區的需求。

paragraphs: 歷史上，美國及其他我們營運國家的總體經濟活動與就業水平，已顯著影響聘僱服務的 demand。在經濟成長期間，僱主通常會先增加臨時員工，再聘僱全職員工。然而，當經濟活動下降時，許多僱主會先減少使用臨時員工，再裁員全職員工。客戶對實際或預期經濟狀況的反應，包括與市場狀況、勞動供給、國際貿易政策及通貨膨脹相關的觀感，可能會負面影響客戶行為。歷史上，總體經濟活動的重大變化，已 disproportionately 影響聘僱產業的交易量。我們可能無法完全受益於經濟活動增加的時期，若我們遭遇勞動力供給不足的情況。我們也可能在經濟衰退期間，面臨更激烈的價格競爭壓力與較慢的客戶付款速度。我們營運美國的業務所產生的收入與獲利，佔了相當大的比例。美國或其他我們營運國家若發生重大經濟衰退，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
我們的普通股市場價格可能面臨顯著波動。我們認為許多因素，包括一些超出我們控制範圍的因素，會對我們普通股的市場價格產生重大影響。這些因素包括：
•我們每季營運結果的實際或預期變動；•我們或競爭對手宣佈新服務；
•與戰略合作關係、收購或出售相關的公告；•證券分析師對財務預測的變動；
•總體經濟狀況的變動；•實際或預期的法律與政府規範變動；
